title: Panel regression for the GDP of the Central and Eastern European countries using time-varying coefficients
hypothesis: H1 time-varying effects concentrate 2008 COVID, H2 private debt strong adverse correlate post-2008, H3 private debt dynamics explain Baltic divergence post-2008
data_sources: Eurostat PPP price level indices real expenditure PPS EU27 2020 100
World Bank FDI net inflows %GDP Trade %GDP GCF %GDP
Eurostat ESTAT Central Government debt %GDP tipspd20 Private debt consolidated %GDP
sample: Panel of 11 CEE EU-acceding countries: Bulgaria, Czechia, Estonia, Croatia, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia. Observed annually from 1995 to 2024. Regressors X1-X7 measured in levels lagged t-1 for 1995-2023 (T=29 per country). Dependent variable Δy_{i,t}=X1_{i,t}-X1_{i,t-1} for intervals 1996-2024 (T=29). Pooled n = N×T = 11×29 = 319 yearly cross-sections N=11 each year, d=7 regressors, df = N-d-1 =3. No missing years stated.
method: Step 1: Define Δy_{i,t}=x_{i,t,1}-x_{i,t-1,1} (X1 = GDP/pc PPS EU27=100) for t=1996-2024. Regressors X1-X7 as in Table variables: X1 GDP/pc PPS level lagged t-1 Eurostat, X2 Price level index EU27=100 level lagged t-1 Eurostat, X3 Accumulated FDI net inflows cum. %GDP level lagged t-1 World Bank, X4 Trade %GDP level lagged t-1 World Bank, X5 Accumulated GCF cum. %GDP level lagged t-1 World Bank, X6 Central Government debt %GDP level lagged t-1 Eurostat, X7 Private debt consolidated %GDP level lagged t-1 Eurostat.

Step 2: Pooled standardization z_{i,t,j}=(x_{i,t,j}-μ_j)/σ_j with μ_j=1/(NT)∑x, σ_j^2=1/(NT-1)∑(x-μ_j)^2 over NT=319, compute pooled correlation matrix Ω = W Λ W', construct orthogonal regressors p_{i,t,k}=∑_j W_{j,k} z_{i,t,j} k=1..d=7 retaining all components; by construction (1/(NT-1))∑ p_k p_l = λ_k δ_{kℓ}.

Step 3: Year-by-year OLS cross-section LRVC in P-space Δy_{i,t}=α_t^P+∑_{k=1}^d γ_{t-1,k} p_{i,t-1,k}+e_{i,t} on N=11 per year for t=1996-2024 (29 regressions). Recover original scale β_{t-1,j}=1/σ_j ∑_k W_{j,k} γ_{t-1,k}, α_t=α_t^P-∑_j μ_j β_{t-1,j}. Compute per-year R2, AdjR2=1-(1-R2)(n-1)/(n-d-1), residual SD, F-statistic, SE via delta method through linear back-transformation.

Step 4: Component decomposition Δy_{i,t,j}=α_t/d+β_{t-1,j} x_{i,t-1,j}, cumulative κ_{i,t,j}=GDP1995/d+∑_{τ=1996}^t Δy_{i,τ,j}, total κ sum to GDP, relative private debt λ(t)=sgn(κ_{i,t,7}) κ_{i,t,7}^2/∑_j κ_{i,t,j}^2. Full regressed GDP Regr.Full uses accumulated Δy^{fr} replacing empirical x_{t-1,1}. Accumulated error e_{i,t}^a=∑_{τ=1996}^t e_{i,τ}=GDP Regr - GDP Data.

Step 5: Diagnostics: pooled residuals e_{i,t} descriptives (mean, SD, median, Q25, Q75, IQR, IQR/SD vs theoretical 1.35, RMSE/MAE vs 1.25), Jarque-Bera normality test, Bartlett heteroskedasticity test for equal variances across 29 yearly cross-sections (B statistic df=28), variance ratio (max SD/min SD)^2.
